question: Does the 2014-2015 Agusan Marsh floodplain-lake study provide species records for each named lake, and can its reported fishery diet statement support natural-prey information?

source.citation: Jumawan, J. C., and Seronay, R. A. (2017). Length-Weight Relationships of Fishes in Eight Floodplain Lakes of Agusan Marsh, Philippines. Philippine Journal of Science, 146(1), 95-99.
source.access: The official Philippine Journal of Science article record and abstract were reviewed. Normal direct requests to the publisher full-text page and the third-party Paperzz page returned HTTP 403; detailed methods and tables were read from the search-indexed Paperzz full-text result, not from a retrieved PDF. A separate NAST Transactions abstract with the same title was also reviewed. No access challenge was bypassed; no table, figure, map, or source PDF is retained.

studyContext.fieldPeriod: The journal article reports sampling from January 2014 through January 2015.
studyContext.sampleMethods: The paper says fish samples were either purchased from local community fish buyers or caught by resident fisher partners, then measured and sorted. It does not provide a row-level purchased-versus-caught flag or voucher accession numbers in the reviewed text.
studyContext.siteResolution: The article pools its reported species table across the eight named floodplain lakes. The table's parenthetical numeric codes refer to fishing gears, not lake identifiers; no taxon-by-lake presence matrix was located. No exact sampling-station geometry was copied.
studyContext.scopeAndVersion: The PJS article abstract reports 16 fish species from eight lakes. A separate NAST Transactions abstract with the same title also reports 16 species and the same field period, but gives different length-weight coefficient range and mean values from the PJS article. No correction or version relationship was found; do not combine the numerical results across versions.
studyContext.humanFoodVersusFishDiet: The journal abstract says many introduced fishes were part of the diet of marsh residents and the fish-eating public. This describes human food use, not fish stomach contents, natural prey, or bait suitability. The paper does not supply taxon-specific fish-diet observations for Bangwit's diet feature.
studyContext.taxonomyAndStatus: The table uses source identifications and native/introduced labels informed by older references. No current taxonomic, conservation, or introduction-status crosswalk was performed; source names and classifications are not copied into app data.
studyContext.reuse: No article-specific reuse license was found in the reviewed PJS page, full-text copy, or NAST abstract. The PJS Author's Guide says accepted authors sign a copyright-transfer form, but does not grant reuse of this specific article. Rights remain unverified.

countAudit.note: The PJS journal abstract and NAST conference abstract share the title, authors, reported sampling window, and 16-species/eight-lake scope, but their length-weight parameter summaries differ. No correction, version lineage, taxon-by-lake matrix, or sample-type crosswalk was found. The numerical versions remain separate and are not reanalyzed here.

interpretation.safeSummary: This historical study reports fish samples obtained from eight named Agusan Marsh floodplain lakes during 2014-2015 by purchase from local buyers or catch with resident fisher partners. Its table pools taxon records across the lakes and does not identify each taxon's lake or whether the sample was directly caught versus purchased. A separate conference abstract with the same title reports conflicting length-weight summaries. The paper's diet wording concerns people consuming fish, not the fish's natural prey.
notSupported: Current presence, abundance, catchability, safe harvest, or a complete present-day checklist for Agusan Marsh or any one of its eight lakes.
Assigning any table taxon to one named lake or a sampling point from the pooled table.
Treating every fish record as a direct specimen capture, since purchased and fisher-caught samples are not separated by taxon.
Using the source's historical native/introduced labels as current taxonomic or conservation status.
Species-specific natural prey, gut-content diet, or bait recommendations from the human-food statement.
Current water quality, safety, legal access, or fishing rules.
interpretation.productUseIfEvidenceAndRightsAreResolved: A future historical research note can describe the named eight-lake study scope and sampling period. Lake-specific species display requires an independent taxon-by-lake record or voucher/source crosswalk and current taxonomic review; any reuse requires permission or verified item-level terms.

qualityAndRights.evidenceLevel: Primary journal study metadata and abstract, with detailed methods/table text reviewed through a third-party copy; lake-level taxonomy and collection-source provenance are pooled.
qualityAndRights.reuseStatus: Item-specific rights were not established. The publisher author guide notes a copyright-transfer form for accepted papers; public-app reuse is not approved.
qualityAndRights.handling: This is a short attributed audit. No taxon table, figure, map, coordinates, measurement values, or article image is reproduced. The third-party copy is not treated as permission to reuse the article.
qualityAndRights.separateEvidenceLanes: Historical pooled fishery samples, direct captures, purchased fish, lake-specific occurrence, human food use, natural fish diet, bait suggestions, current water quality, safety, and legal fishing guidance remain separate evidence types.

disposition.reason: The paper does not provide a per-taxon lake assignment or a purchased-versus-caught provenance flag, the versioned abstracts disagree on numerical results, and reuse terms for the article were not verified.

nextAction: Continue Caraga's freshwater evidence sweep for a primary survey or voucher dataset that identifies taxa at individual lakes or reaches and distinguishes direct field collection from reported or purchased specimens. Keep this marsh-level study as historical context only.

sources.supports: Official Philippine Journal of Science citation, article abstract, authors, volume, issue, pages, 16-species/eight-lake claim, and human-food-use wording.

Search-indexed third-party full-text result used to review the methods, eight lake names, mixed purchase/capture sampling, pooled species table and lack of per-taxon lake identifiers; direct page request returned HTTP 403.
Separate 2017 NAST Transactions abstract with the same title and authors and a different length-weight parameter summary.
